question: Should OpenClaw accept this always-on 512-row shared-SQLite restart ledger with the proposed stable session fingerprint and actor/device/IP/path/preflight metadata, or must the durable field set and access contract be narrowed before merge?
rationale: Code review can verify redaction, bounded retention, and restart ordering, but it cannot decide which operational identifiers OpenClaw intends to retain durably or whether flexible JSON payloads are an acceptable long-term security and state-model boundary.

options.title: Narrow the durable contract
options.body: Keep restart attribution but replace or tightly whitelist flexible payload fields, omit identifiers that are not essential, and document retention and local access before merge.

options.title: Accept the bounded ledger
options.body: Explicitly approve the current redacted metadata set, stable correlation behavior, 512-row retention, and raw local-database inspection as the intended first contract.

options.title: Use existing diagnostics only
options.body: Pause or close the PR and project restart attribution into the existing diagnostic stability/export surfaces if a separate always-on audit table is not worth the privacy and ownership cost.

recommendation.title: Narrow the durable contract
recommendation.body: Keep restart attribution but replace or tightly whitelist flexible payload fields, omit identifiers that are not essential, and document retention and local access before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The broader metadata-only audit proposal and its stated privacy/retention constraints make this the strongest available product-security routing signal.
